title: Drive VCF Automation machine provisioning through its request tracker
prompt:
Implement the dependency-free, single-file Java client in `VcfAutomationMachineClient.java`. Use only the Java standard library, do not add dependencies, and do not edit any other file.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection of the VCF Automation provisioning API of VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1. VCF Automation, the successor to vRealize Automation and Aria Automation, publishes no specification in VMware's `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository, so this contract is transcribed from the rendered xAPIs reference pages Broadcom publishes for the 'VM Apps Org - Provisioning Service' at developer.broadcom.com, and it says so in its own `source` block. `docs/official_sources.json` records, for every operation, the reference page URL, the operation that page documents and the date it was read. There is no OpenAPI document, repository commit or specification path behind any of it. Use exactly the contract's operationIds `retrieveAuthToken`, `getAboutPage`, `createMachine`, `getRequestTracker` and `getMachine`; do not call another route.

Preserve the supplied public API and its doc comments: `SERVICE_BASE_PATH`, the `OP_*` operationId constants, the `STATUS_*` constants, `DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL`, `DEFAULT_POLL_TIMEOUT`, `Config` and both of its constructors, `Tag`, `MachineRequest` and both of its constructors, `MachineRef`, `ProvisionResult`, `ProvisioningException`, `VcfAutomationApiException`, `RequestFailedException`, `RequestPollTimeoutException`, `VcfAutomationProtocolException`, `VcfAutomationTransportException`, `create`, `apiVersion` and `provision`.

`create` must reject a configuration before anything is sent, with an `IllegalArgumentException`. `Config.baseUrl` must be an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL with a host and no userinfo, path, query or fragment; a bare trailing slash is acceptable. Reject a null or blank `Config.refreshToken`, reject a refresh token that contains an ASCII control character, and reject a non-positive `Config.pollInterval` or `Config.pollTimeout`. A null or blank `Config.machineSelect` means no selector was configured; a non-blank one that contains an ASCII control character or a character that would have to be escaped in a query string is rejected. Default `pollInterval` to 5s, `pollTimeout` to 20m, and `httpClient` to a client with a 30s connect timeout.

Every request target is the origin of `Config.baseUrl` followed by the operation's path, with path parameters substituted. Send `Accept: application/json` on every request, exactly and without parameters. `retrieveAuthToken` is the operation that obtains the token, so it must not carry an `Authorization` header; every other operation sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with the `token` that operation returned, as its reference page instructs. Send `Content-Type: application/json` only on a request that carries an entity.

`apiVersion` is an optional query parameter the reference declares on `retrieveAuthToken`, `createMachine`, `getRequestTracker` and `getMachine`, and its value is not a constant to assume: read it from `getAboutPage`, whose `latestApiVersion` member is the version to use, and send `apiVersion=<latestApiVersion>` on `createMachine`, `getRequestTracker` and `getMachine`. `retrieveAuthToken` runs before any version has been discovered and must carry no query string at all, and `getAboutPage` declares no query parameter so it must carry none either. `$select` is the second optional query parameter of `getMachine`: send it verbatim and only when `Config.machineSelect` was configured, after `apiVersion`, and never with an empty value. The token and the discovered version are obtained once per client and reused by later `provision` calls.

Treat the documented success status as the only success: 202 for `createMachine` and 200 for the other four operations.

`provision` posts a `MachineSpecification` to `/iaas/api/machines`. `name`, `projectId`, `image` and `flavor` are always sent. `description`, `tags`, `customProperties` and `deploymentId` are the optional members: a null or empty value of any of them is the unset case and the member must not appear in the entity at all, rather than being sent as null, as an empty string, as an empty array or as an empty object. Serialise members in the order `name`, `projectId`, `image`, `flavor`, `description`, `tags`, `customProperties`, `deploymentId`, each `Tag` as `key` then `value`, and `customProperties` in the iteration order of the supplied map. Entities are compact JSON with no insignificant whitespace.

Creation is accepted asynchronously with a `RequestTracker`. The status carried by that acceptance reply is not an observation of the outcome and neither are the resources it lists: drive the request to a terminal state with `getRequestTracker` on `/iaas/api/request-tracker/{id}`, sending no body and no `Content-Type`. Poll once immediately after acceptance and then wait `pollInterval` between polls. `INPROGRESS` continues; `FINISHED` and `FAILED` are terminal; stop as soon as a terminal status is read. Once `pollTimeout` has passed since acceptance, give up with a `RequestPollTimeoutException` carrying the request id, the last non-terminal status and the progress read with it.

A request that reaches `FAILED`, or any terminal status other than `FINISHED`, raises a `RequestFailedException` carrying the request id, that status, the tracker's own `message` and its `progress`; no machine may be read afterwards. A `FINISHED` tracker must carry exactly one entry in `resources`, of the documented form `/iaas/api/machines/{id}`; anything else is a `VcfAutomationProtocolException`. Read that machine with `getMachine` and populate `ProvisionResult` with the request id, the tracker's `selfLink`, the terminal status, the tracker's `progress`, the apiVersion in use, the number of `getRequestTracker` calls it took to observe the terminal status, and the machine's `id`, `name`, `powerState`, `address`, `externalId` and `projectId`.

Any status the contract does not document as success raises a `VcfAutomationApiException` carrying the failing operationId, the HTTP status, and the `ServiceErrorResponse` body's `message`, `errorCode` and `serverErrorId`; it carries the request id once one exists and null before that. A request that cannot be delivered, or a reply that cannot be read, raises a `VcfAutomationTransportException` and leaves the calling thread's interrupt status intact. A reply that cannot be understood as the document the contract projects raises a `VcfAutomationProtocolException`. Never place the refresh token, the bearer token or a raw response body in an exception message.

Verify with `java TestMain.java`.

prerequisites.java: 22 or later (the harness uses the multi-file source-code launcher)

source_basis.reason: VCF Automation publishes no API specification in the Apache-2.0 vmware/vcf-api-specs repository, so the contract is derived from the authoritative rendered xAPIs reference instead, and states that plainly.
source_basis.documented_api_title: VMware Aria Automation Assembler IaaS API

scenario: Machine creation is accepted with HTTP 202 and a RequestTracker that must be polled to FINISHED or FAILED before anything is believed: one run provisions two machines on a single client and reuses the token and the discovered apiVersion, one reads the machine with the optional $select selector against a differently versioned service, one is handed an acceptance reply that already reads FINISHED and points at a stale machine and must still poll, one ends FAILED at the datastore and must be reported without reading a machine, and one never leaves INPROGRESS and must give up at the poll deadline.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves the exact request sequence, that apiVersion is discovered from getAboutPage rather than assumed, that $select appears only when configured and never empty, that no Authorization header precedes the token exchange, that entity-less requests carry no Content-Type, and that an unset optional member of MachineSpecification is omitted entirely rather than sent as null, empty or an empty collection.
